ogTitle: Top 10 Popular Restaurants in Yasothon 2026 — Eat Like a Local in Yasothon
ogDesc: Old-town café, original boat noodles, authentic Isan duck laab, and the city's iconic lod chong — 10 Yasothon restaurants locals actually eat at, with prices and eating tips.
eyebrow: Eat Like a Local in Yasothon · Updated 2026
intro: Yasothon is a small city that eats far better than its size suggests — from a self-roasting café in a century-old building, to the original boat noodle shop, right through to authentic Isan duck laab you simply cannot find anywhere else. We've pulled together 10 restaurants that Yasothon locals keep coming back to: relaxed chill spots, serious main-meal places, and the city's iconic sweet. Work down the list one restaurant at a time.
chips: ☕ Old-town café in Baan Sing Tha

blocks.html:
To understand Yasothon at its core, start with what the city eats. The old-town neighbourhood of Baan Sing Tha is lined with Sino-European shophouses that have become home to cafés and long-running food shops. You can walk and photograph the architecture while pausing to sip fresh milk, eat warm steamed bread, and stroll at your own pace. Beyond the old quarter, out in the city and on the bypass road, you find bold Isan flavours taken seriously: laab, fresh-herb salad, papaya salad, and grilled fish the way Yasothon locals actually eat them — alongside boat noodles and Ubon-style guay jab that have been passed down through family recipes for a long time. The eating atmosphere in Yasothon isn't polished, but it's warm and genuine in the Isan way that brings people back.

This list includes the restaurants that Yasothon residents call the city's signature spots: Vachi, a specialty coffee café in an old building that self-roasts its beans and bakes fresh pastries every day; Singh Nom Sod, an ancient-recipe fresh-milk shop in Baan Sing Tha that draws a crowd all day; Puay Boat Noodles Yasothon, the original recipe with the rich, full broth that people say needs no seasoning; and Mae Aom Duck Laab, the pure-meat duck laab with proper seasoning that is a fixture of this city. For noodle lovers there's also Lert Rot guay jab noodles. For dessert, Khao Wan by Chef Uan closes the meal with lod chong in fresh coconut milk fragrant with pandan leaf — a Baan Sing Tha staple sold here for years. Eat through all 10 and you've tasted the full range of what Yasothon is made of. Let's start.

blocks.name: Vachi (Vachi Coffeebar & Bistro)
blocks.signature: Self-roasted coffee, matcha latte, cheesecake and freshly baked pastries
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Yasothon local where to meet a friend for a proper coffee and "Vachi" (Vachi Coffeebar & Bistro) is almost always the first name up. This is a specialty coffee café with a loft-style interior that has become the regular meeting point for Yasothon people — now running three branches: the main Chaeng Sanit branch (flagship), the Uthai Ramrit branch in the city centre, and the Old Town branch in Baan Sing Tha. Great for anyone who wants a quiet spot to sit, work, or have a meeting in air conditioning with free wi-fi, plenty of tables, and convenient parking.

The coffee that enthusiasts talk about most is the in-house roasted, in-house-formula blend — rotating beans from multiple origins. For black coffee drinkers, try the iced Americano or cappuccino with latte art from a barista team that has placed in national coffee competition. For non-coffee drinkers there's a matcha latte made with imported Japanese powder, cocoa, and a house Thai tea formula. Finish with freshly baked pastries: cheesecake, croissant, and rocky road cake that pair naturally with the coffee. Drinks start at around 40 THB; most items stay under 100 THB — comfortable range.

The charm of Vachi is its playful interior design. International reviewers have called it "quirky," with photogenic details like a wrench repurposed as a door handle. Many people say the coffee and cake feel like a big-city café, while the staff are friendly and the music is soft enough to stay for hours. The Old Town branch has a raw industrial feel — exposed brick and recycled sheet metal — distinctly different from the main branch.

Good to know: opening hours vary slightly by branch. The Chaeng Sanit branch runs roughly 08:00–17:30 (weekends from 09:00) and closes fairly early in the afternoon. If you want a long sit, go midday or early afternoon. On holidays you may wait for a table. LINE MAN delivery is available if you'd rather not come in. If you're visiting Yasothon and want one good café, Vachi is a reliable call.
blocks.bestFor: Working / afternoon coffee with a friend

blocks.name: Singh Nom Sod
blocks.signature: Pure fresh milk, ancient-recipe coffee, toast and steamed bread, khao soi, Ubon guay jab, braised pork curry rice with thick egg
blocks.descHtml:
Come to Yasothon and want somewhere to sit with a warm glass of fresh milk in an old wooden-house setting — Singh Nom Sod is the first name locals think of. The shop is in the Baan Sing Tha old-town neighbourhood, directly opposite the City Pillar Shrine — a traditional Chinese wooden house that has kept the atmosphere of the original trading community intact. Good for café-lovers who want a vintage feel, people looking for a relaxed morning meal, or a group of friends who want to sit long from mid-morning into the evening.

The most-ordered items are the pure, smooth fresh milk — easy to drink — and the ancient-recipe coffee that pairs naturally with toast and steamed bread in various toppings. The savoury side goes further than a typical café: there's khao soi, clear-broth Ubon guay jab, and braised pork curry rice with thick egg that reviewers consistently say has beautifully tender pork and a smooth, drinkable broth. The overall flavour leans toward the comforting and homestyle — well-rounded, not aggressively seasoned, comfortable for all ages.

What makes this place memorable is the atmosphere. There's both an indoor zone and outdoor tables that catch a nice breeze; the evening light is beautiful for photos. Several reviews mention that the restaurant often has fragrant bael-fruit tea on the side for a slow sip. Pricing is friendly — from tens of baht, most savoury items still under 100 THB per dish. Good value for a comfortable meal.

Good to know: the shop opens nearly all day from morning to evening, around 08:00–21:00 daily. Weekends draw a fair crowd because it's both a local gathering spot and a stop for tourists walking the old town. Street parking out front. If it's your first meal of a Yasothon trip and you want both good food and a beautiful old setting, this restaurant fits perfectly.
mustOrder: Ancient-recipe coffee + toast and steamed bread
Braised pork curry rice with thick egg
blocks.bestFor: Breakfast / relaxed sit in the old town
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: café · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Baan Khun Ya
blocks.signature: Soft-shell crab salad loaded with ingredients, sunflower sprout papaya salad, Baan Khun Ya omelette, fresh-milk cake and custard cake, shabu
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Khun Ya is the first restaurant Yasothon people think of when relatives come to visit or when they want a proper relaxed meal. The main branch is on Rattanakhet Road in the city centre, near Kluamai Hotel, with a second riverside branch for those who prefer an open-air setting. It's been open long enough to have become a memory for multiple generations. Good for families with children, parents bringing kids, or groups of friends who want a long, comfortable sit in the air conditioning.

Most-ordered items include the soft-shell crab salad packed with bold seasoning, sunflower sprout papaya salad served with prawns and squid for a fresh crunch, and the Baan Khun Ya omelette — fluffy and signature, described by many as a must-order. For hot dishes there's shabu and suki by the pot. The desserts are the real trump card: soft white fresh-milk cake, smooth perfectly-sweet custard cake, and colourful jelly cakes that many people buy as takeaway gifts.

On flavour, most reviews praise the fresh cooking, generous portions, and the range of both savoury and sweet in one place. Pantip reviews have given full marks for taste and value. Some reviews note directly that with such a long menu, certain dishes are more consistent than others — sticking to the standout dishes is the safer move. Per-head cost around 100–250 THB, which is accessible for a family meal.

Open daily from about 07:00 through the evening. Accepts cards. Plenty of seating for large groups. Good to know: holidays and evenings get fairly crowded — for a larger group, calling ahead is the smarter move. And save room for dessert, because that's what keeps people coming back.
mustOrder: Soft-shell crab salad loaded with ingredients
blocks.bestFor: Relaxed family meal and fresh-milk cake desserts
blocks.spice: Spice adjustable — papaya salad and yam are medium-hot

blocks.name: Krua Rachawadi Food & Drink
blocks.signature: Grilled fish, battered fried prawns, liang vegetable soup, papaya salad and chilli dip, bold Isan food
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Rachawadi Food & Drink is the big Thai–Isan restaurant of Yasothon city, tucked behind Lotus Yasothon on Chaeng Sanit Soi 1, all the way to the end of the lane. It's the restaurant Yasothon people think of when welcoming out-of-town guests, bringing the family for a big meal, or getting a group together. The restaurant splits into several seating zones: an open outdoor garden zone with a breeze, a veranda zone, and an air-conditioned room — your pick depending on the weather and how many people you have. The menu runs to pages and covers both Thai and bold Isan cuisine. Coming alone and ordering a single dish works fine; coming in a group of ten and filling the table is even better.

Most-ordered items are a large grilled fish — sweet, easy-to-separate flesh, served with a punchy jaew dipping sauce — and battered fried prawns that come out well-crispy and plump. For hot soup, the liang soup with mixed vegetables is fragrant with peppercorn in just the right balance. For the Isan side, order papaya salad and fresh-vegetable chilli dip, then add fried fermented pork or stir-fried wild boar to round out the table. For larger groups, a seafood hot pot or snakehead fish pae sa is a great shared centre dish. Most reviews agree: the food comes in generous portions, overall flavour is solid, and the price is good value.

Mid-range pricing for a special meal — around 251–500 THB per person for a full spread; ordering as a group makes the per-head cost even better. Easy to find using Lotus Yasothon as the reference point. Convenient parking. Open daily 11:00–22:00, kitchen closes around 21:00 — if you're coming for dinner, allow a little time.

The reason this restaurant ranks as one of Yasothon's most popular is that it ticks all the boxes at once: a long menu, comfortable seating, and a genuine ability to handle large groups. Google reviews hold steady at 4.4 stars. Good to know: evenings on holidays and during the Bun Bang Fai Rocket Festival get crowded — call ahead for a table if you're coming in a group. Delivery is also available.
blocks.bestFor: Welcoming guests, family meals, large groups

blocks.name: Puay Boat Noodles Yasothon (Original)
blocks.area: Surawet Alley (entered from Chaeng Sanit Road), Nai Mueang Subdistrict, Mueang Yasothon District, Yasothon Province
blocks.signature: Pork and beef boat noodles with rich, full broth, crispy pork crackling, unlimited vegetables
blocks.descHtml:
Anyone stopping in Yasothon who wants a deep, hot, rich bowl of boat noodles — Puay Boat Noodles Yasothon (Original), in Surawet Alley off Chaeng Sanit Road in the Nai Mueang neighbourhood, is the shop locals talk about most. This is a single-location shop, no branches, running long enough to become a household name in Yasothon. Good for a quick morning or midday meal, solo or with family — the restaurant is open-plan, plenty of tables, fast service, comfortable at your own pace.

The must-order is the boat noodles — available in both pork and beef. Many people particularly love the nam tok thin noodles with mixed beef and pork: the house broth is rich and deeply fragrant with spices all the way through. People who've eaten here consistently say the meat is tender, the broth is rounded and balanced, and you don't need to season it. The crispy pork crackling sprinkled on top adds satisfying chew, and fresh vegetables are free refill. Lod chong is also on the menu to finish on a sweet note.

Very wallet-friendly — starting at around 50 THB per bowl; most bowls stay under 100 THB. Comfortable, easy local restaurant atmosphere. Around noon the crowd picks up and the car park fills visibly — proof it's genuinely popular. Open from around 08:00 to 16:00. If you plan to eat here, go in the morning to mid-afternoon, because items run out early.

Good to know: the shop closes fairly early, and arriving late in the afternoon risks finding nothing left. As a smaller neighbourhood restaurant it may also have its own occasional rest days — calling ahead is worth it. For anyone who loves rich, full-bodied boat noodles with proper seasoning and wants to taste the original recipe of Yasothon city, this is the stop to put on the map.
mustOrder: Beef boat noodles with rich broth
Nam tok thin noodles (mixed beef and pork)
blocks.bestFor: Morning or midday noodle meal, budget-friendly
blocks.hours: 08:00–16:00 (come in the morning–before midday, items run out early)
blocks.spice: Adjustable — broth is rich and rounded, not aggressively hot; season yourself

blocks.name: Hug na Yasothon Pizza & Spaghetti (Hug)
blocks.signature: Pizza, spaghetti, Italian-style dishes in a semi-Western atmosphere
blocks.descHtml:
Come to Yasothon and want a break from papaya salad and laab? Hug na Yasothon Pizza & Spaghetti is a small Italian restaurant in the city that consistently surprises visitors — because most people don't expect a small city like this to have hand-made fresh pasta, wood-fired pizza, and wine served alongside a proper evening meal. Good for people who want Western food in a relaxed setting, couples looking for a special meal, or a group of friends who want to sit and take their time.

The dishes most talked about are the fresh pasta — a Pantip review praised the hand-made noodles as very good — followed by oven-roasted chicken with potatoes that reviewers found impressively tender, and hot wood-fired pizza. For those who want to go all out, order a white wine with cheese and fruit to start, then move to red wine with the main in proper Italian fashion. The chef handles Italian cooking to a high standard — the consistent reviewer verdict is "excellent" and not a wasted visit.

The atmosphere is comfortably semi-Western, easy to sit in and enjoy at your own pace. Reviews note that evening tables fill quickly. Prices are accessible for Italian food — roughly 330–840 THB per person depending on what you order. Sharing dishes across a group with a bottle of red wine comes in around the low two-thousands, which most reviewers consider good value for what you get.

Located in Mueang Yasothon District, open daily 09:00–21:00. This restaurant is popular because it's one of the very few Italian places in the city that makes fresh pasta by hand and controls the seasoning consistently. Good to know: on holiday evenings it can get crowded — for a group, calling ahead to book a table is worth the call.
blocks.bestFor: Special evening meal for a couple or group, wanting a change of cuisine

blocks.name: Lert Rot Ubon–Vietnamese Guay Jab, Yasothon Branch
blocks.signature: Vietnamese-style guay jab — springy fresh noodles, slow-cooked pork-bone broth, loaded toppings
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to taste Vietnamese-style guay jab at its roots, Yasothon is the city to come to — the old-town neighbourhood of Baan Sing Tha has a long-established Vietnamese-heritage community, so Viet food became a local flavour here long ago. Lert Rot Ubon–Vietnamese Guay Jab, Yasothon Branch is the long-running shop locals think of first when they want a bowl of fully-loaded Vietnamese guay jab in the morning or mid-morning. Good for anyone visiting the old town who wants a first meal that's filling and genuinely local.

The must-order is the fresh Vietnamese guay jab noodles: hand-kneaded from rice-flour dough into smooth, springy sheets, then topped with pork broth slow-cooked from bones until sweet and clear — the fragrance of peppercorn and coriander root carries from a distance. The bowl comes packed: minced pork, pork sausage, boiled egg, fried pork scratchings, spring onion and coriander, fried shallots. Squeeze in a little lime to round the flavour up. People who've eaten here consistently say the broth is smooth and balanced without being heavy from MSG. For those who want heat, chilli flakes and chilli vinegar are on the table to season yourself.

Very reasonable price — a bowl of Vietnamese guay jab is around 60–80 THB. Adding extra pork sausage or a Viet-style snack on the side still won't hurt the wallet. The restaurant atmosphere is a plain, simple shophouse in the local style — not decorated, but clean and fast. Located in Mueang Yasothon, close to Baan Sing Tha old town, easy to continue walking the neighbourhood afterwards.

One note: shops of this type tend to sell out faster mid-morning. If you want the full selection of toppings, come before noon. The fresh noodles of Vietnamese guay jab are best eaten hot — eat at the table rather than taking it away. Anyone passing through Yasothon who hasn't tried the local Vietnamese guay jab has missed one of the city's signature flavours.
mustOrder: Vietnamese guay jab with fresh noodles
blocks.bestFor: First morning meal in the old town of Yasothon

blocks.name: Mae Aom Duck Laab (Mahalap Laab Yaso)
blocks.signature: Pure duck meat laab with full seasoning, crispy fried duck, tom saep duck hot pot, papaya salad
blocks.descHtml:
Anyone visiting Yasothon who wants genuinely original duck laab will find that Mae Aom Duck Laab (Mahalap Laab Yaso) is where the locals go first. This is a plain neighbourhood restaurant tucked into a lane, on the opposite side of the Yasothon Hospital intersection — drive into the lane about 1 kilometre, on the right. Shaded by trees with a comfortable breeze passing through. Good for people who want bold Isan flavours without a dress code — sit and relax with friends or family without any rush.

The dish everyone orders is pure duck meat laab with full seasoning, bold and old-recipe spiced. Reviewers say the duck here has no gamey smell at all, and is thoroughly enjoyable. The crispy fried duck is the next star — fried through until the whole piece is crispy, almost every part chewable, perfectly salty. Tom saep duck (duck hot pot) has tender meat fragrant with lemongrass; the hot broth is easy to drink through. Finish with papaya salad alongside the duck dishes and you have a complete meal in one sitting.

Extremely friendly pricing — duck laab and fried duck are 80 THB per dish, duck hot pot is 70 THB, papaya salad 40 THB, averaging about 101–250 THB per person. Easy on the wallet. Open daily 08:00–16:00. Great for a midday or first meal on arrival in Yasothon. For anyone wanting authentic Isan food at an accessible price, this is the stop.

One small note: the restaurant is deep in a lane and the sign is not prominent — use GPS coordinates to find it easily. Because it's a garden-style outdoor restaurant, expect the occasional fly that comes with fried and roasted duck restaurants. Takeaway is an option, but eating hot at the restaurant is worth the drive in.
mustOrder: Pure duck meat laab with full seasoning
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, duck laab enthusiasts
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: papaya salad · Vyacheslav Argenberg / Wikimedia (CC BY 4.0)

blocks.name: Khao Wan by Chef Uan
blocks.area: Tat Thong Subdistrict, Mueang Yasothon District, Yasothon Province
blocks.cuisine: Thai sweets / desserts and Isan food
blocks.signature: Lod chong in fresh pandan-scented coconut milk, served alongside bold Isan food in one place
blocks.descHtml:
Yasothon has been famous for lod chong for a long time — it has become the city's signature souvenir that visitors from other provinces seek out. Khao Wan by Chef Uan is one of the restaurants that has taken this local sweet and made it easy to enjoy any day. The restaurant is in the Tat Thong neighbourhood, behind Wat Thung, in Mueang Yasothon District — a small, warm, neighbourhood-style shop, open daily from mid-morning to evening. Easy to pull over and park for a stop, with a relaxed, unhurried atmosphere.

The star of the shop is lod chong in coconut milk: in-house pandan-fragrant lod chong noodles with a springy, smooth texture, topped with freshly cooked coconut milk that is rich, fragrant, and perfectly sweet without being cloying. Add a scoop of shaved ice for an instant cool-down from the Isan heat. For a fully loaded version, order the mixed dessert in fresh coconut milk — lod chong, sago, and several other Thai sweets in one cup. This is a dessert made with care, and the flavour recalls the handmade sweets from the neighbourhood.

What makes this restaurant more than a regular lod chong shop is its name — Khao Wan (savoury and sweet) — which says exactly what it is: a place with both savoury and sweet dishes in one stop. The owner is skilled at bold Isan food: papaya salad, laab, and rice-box sets for events and merit-making meals. Perfect for a group that wants a full Isan savoury main followed by cold sweet dessert without moving tables — one stop, one meal, all done.

Khao Wan by Chef Uan is a relaxed stop for anyone who wants to taste Yasothon's local lod chong in a real, seated, sit-down restaurant rather than just a takeaway stall. If you're visiting the old town of Yasothon, doing merit at Wat Thung or exploring the Tat Thong neighbourhood, and want a local sweet to cool down, this is the pin to drop.
mustOrder: Lod chong in fresh coconut milk, fragrant pandan
Mixed dessert in fresh coconut milk (loaded)
blocks.bestFor: Stopping for local cold sweets, or a full savoury-and-sweet meal while exploring the old town of Yasothon
blocks.zone: Tat Thong–behind Wat Thung, Yasothon city
blocks.foodType: Desserts / lod chong–Thai sweets and Isan savoury food
blocks.spice: Choose your level — desserts are not spicy; Isan savoury items are spiced to order
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: Thai sweets · Ilya Plekhanov / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak
blocks.signature: Bold, punchy Isan food, wild-game dishes, fried fish, fish tom yum
blocks.descHtml:
If you want bold, punchy Isan food in a relaxed, shaded garden setting — Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak is the restaurant Yasothon people like to bring the crowd to. The restaurant is on the bypass road in Yasothon city (behind Krua Binla), laid out as a lush green garden with both open-air shaded zones and air-conditioned rooms, a small waterfall and a windmill for decoration. Good for a family or a large group who want to sit comfortably without rushing.

Most-ordered items are Isan and wild-game dishes with bold seasoning: garlic-fried frog that comes out crisp and fragrant, fried fermented pork, duck laab that reviewers say has good flavour with no gamey smell, clear-broth kang fish tom yum with a punchy, well-balanced heat, and stir-fried wild boar with chilli paste. There's also a range of freshwater fish dishes. Order alongside hot sticky rice for a complete shared table.

Multiple reviews say the food is full-flavoured, well-seasoned, and generous in portion. What stands out is the restaurant owner's attentive service — sometimes even serving seasonal fruit as a finisher. Pricing is around 101–250 THB per person, which is good value for the quantity and atmosphere. Accepts cards. Convenient parking. Free wi-fi.

Open daily 10:00–21:00. Holiday evenings get fairly crowded — for a larger group, calling ahead to reserve a table gives peace of mind. Signature dishes are cooked fresh to order, so some items may take a little time; accept the wait for the freshness. A worthwhile restaurant when you want Isan food, atmosphere, and real outdoor space all in one.
blocks.bestFor: Family or group meal in a shaded garden setting
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: tom yum · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Yasothon

items.title: Getting Around
items.text: Most restaurants are in the city centre and the Baan Sing Tha old-town neighbourhood — walking between cafés and old buildings is easy. For restaurants out on the bypass road like Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak, you need a vehicle. Grab is sparse and slow in Yasothon; renting a car or using a private vehicle gives you the most freedom.

items.title: Carry Cash
items.text: Street-food stalls and dessert shops like lod chong, boat noodles, and duck laab mostly take cash or PromptPay QR. Keep small bills on hand. Cafés and sit-down restaurants typically accept transfers.

items.title: Time Your Visits
items.text: Midday restaurants like Puay boat noodles and Mae Aom duck laab open from morning and close in the afternoon — go late and things may run out. Cafés on holiday middays get crowded. For a good table at a relaxed pace, come before noon.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: No tipping obligation at general Thai restaurants. Street-food stalls — pay the listed price. At sit-down restaurants with attentive table service, leaving coins or rounding up slightly is a welcome gesture, never a fixed expectation.

items.title: Language and Menus
items.text: Most local restaurant menus are in Thai only. Non-Thai speakers can photograph the menu and use Google Translate, or point at photos. Cafés like Vachi and the Italian restaurant Hug are easier to communicate in and have menus that are readable without Thai.

items.title: About Spice
items.text: Isan food in Yasothon is genuinely bold and hot — especially laab, fresh-herb salad, and papaya salad. If you can't handle heat well, tell the restaurant 'phet noi' (a little spicy) or 'mai phet' (not spicy). Most restaurants will adjust. Cafés and desserts are completely non-spicy — good starting points.

blocks.title: Planning a Full Day of Eating in Yasothon
blocks.html:
If you have one day, organise it in rounds. Start the morning at a café — Vachi for self-roasted coffee and fresh-baked pastries, or Singh Nom Sod in Baan Sing Tha for fresh milk and steamed bread, then walk the old buildings for photos straight after.

Midday, go for a hot bowl at Puay Boat Noodles Yasothon in Surawet Alley — opens until afternoon, but items go early. If you want another style of noodle, Lert Rot Vietnamese guay jab is in the old-town neighbourhood too. For dinner, go for bold Isan food at Krua Rachawadi behind Lotus, or the garden setting of Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak on the bypass road with the open-air ambience. Don't forget to close with lod chong at Baan Sing Tha — fragrant pandan coconut milk at just a few tens of baht a cup, the best deal in town.

blocks.text: Eating through multiple meals in Yasothon is far easier with a well-located overnight stay. Choose a city-centre place near Baan Sing Tha — walk to cafés and dessert shops with ease. Check latest availability and prices before you travel.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Yasothon is the most famous?
faq.a: By local buzz, Vachi (Vachi Coffeebar & Bistro) is the most talked-about café for self-roasted coffee and fresh-baked pastries. For serious savoury food, Puay Boat Noodles Yasothon (original recipe) and Singh Nom Sod in Baan Sing Tha are the shops locals keep returning to.

faq.q: What are the signature things to eat in Yasothon?
faq.a: Must-tries include authentic Isan duck laab the way Mae Aom makes it — pure meat, full seasoning; Puay's rich, full-broth boat noodles; fresh milk and steamed bread at Singh Nom Sod; and Baan Sing Tha lod chong — pandan-fragrant coconut milk as the perfect sweet finish to a meal.

faq.q: How much does eating in Yasothon cost per meal?
faq.a: Very wallet-friendly. Desserts like lod chong start from 15–35 THB per cup. Puay boat noodles run 50–80 THB per bowl. Mae Aom duck laab is 70–80 THB per dish. Sit-down Isan restaurants for a full table at Krua Rachawadi or Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak come to around 101–500 THB per person depending on what you order.

faq.q: Do Yasothon restaurants require advance booking?
faq.a: Most are walk-in — especially street-food stalls and cafés. On long weekends or during the Bun Bang Fai Rocket Festival, sit-down restaurants like Krua Rachawadi and Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak can get crowded. If you're coming in a large group, calling ahead is the safer move.

faq.q: Which restaurants in Yasothon are open for evening or late dining?
faq.a: Isan sit-down restaurants for a long evening dinner — Krua Rachawadi and Suan Ahan Rabieng Rak — both stay open until around 21:00–22:00. Cafés like Vachi and boat noodles at Puay focus on the midday window and close in the afternoon. If you're targeting the midday restaurants, go before mid-afternoon to avoid missing out.
